description: Full application for residential development on the School Paddock, land off Hays Lane, Sageston, Tenby, Pembrokeshire SA70 8SQ (applicant Carew Castle Estate, agent Harries Planning Design Management, Job No. 2026). Proposed phase of 12 detached 3-bed market houses with one adoptable dead-end access road off Hays Lane. Status: proposed, undetermined (no decision notice reviewed) — confidence is sense_check, not approved_unit_count, for that reason. Held out: not used to tune any engine parameter, run once after the restriction bars-semantics fix (Restriction.bars: 'buildings' | 'everything') and reported as-is.

restrictions.label: Nothing here
restrictions.source: Planning, Design and Access Statement (18 May 2026), 'Figure 5 – Proposed Block Plan' (1:200): a long hatched infiltration-basin strip runs the full width of the site along the northern boundary, annotated 'PROPOSED SURFACE DRAINS TO DISCHARGE TO INFILTRATION BASIN' / 'INSTALLED BENEATH BASE OF BASIN'. The Statement's own text confirms this: 'a large portion of the north of the site has been used to create a SuDS feature to comply with [SAB] requirements' and 'new hedgerow is proposed to the rear of the site, to create separation between the SuDS area and the dwellings.' bars="everything" (Nothing here): this is an infiltration basin, not a buried easement — nothing (road, turning head or building) should be sited on it. Traced by eye from the same 1:200 drawing as boundaryBng (pixel-measured, area-anchored — see this fixture's own notes field for the method and its limits), so its position relative to the boundary is consistent with the drawing, even though neither is georeferenced.

expectedUnitsMethod: Applicant's proposed total, read directly from the Planning, Design and Access Statement (18 May 2026): 'This Statement supports a full application for the development of 12 residential units...' and the Application Form's own Q3/Q16 (residential development, gain of units). All 12 are detached, 3-bedroom houses across 3 house types (Type A/B/C, Type A slightly smaller) — no flats, no bungalows. NOT a confirmed LPA-approved count: no decision notice was found among the documents reviewed this session — confidence is sense_check, not approved_unit_count, for that reason, exactly as with gibbas-way-pembroke.
notes:
HELD-OUT FIXTURE, not tuned on: added and run once, after the restriction bars-semantics fix (Restriction.bars), with no engine parameter changed to chase this fixture's own number.

File identification: the Drive file actually named 'PA-Planning Block Plan-25062026' (test-sites/source/sageston/PA-Planning_Block_Plan-25062026_ExistingSitePlan.pdf) turned out, on inspection, to be Drawing 07 Rev A, titled 'EXISTING SITE PLAN' — the pre-development topographical survey, not a layout with plots. The actual 1:200 proposed block plan (house footprints, road, SuDS basin) is 'Figure 5 – Proposed Block Plan' embedded inside the Planning, Design and Access Statement (test-sites/source/sageston/PA-Planning_Design_and_Access_Statement-25062026.pdf, page 3) — one of the three files the user named, so used directly rather than opening a fourth file. boundaryBng and the SuDS restriction were both traced from that embedded 1:200 image, not from the existing-site-plan PDF (which has no proposed layout to trace from, but was still opened and used for general site context — existing levels, trees, services — consistent with the user's instruction).

Boundary tracing method — same family as Meads, NOT as good as Gibbas Way: neither 'block plan' PDF carries OS grid references or a printed dimension string, only a stated 'Scale - 1:200' and a graphic scale bar with no numbers legible at the resolution available. The boundary (7 vertices) and the SuDS basin (4 vertices) were pixel-traced by eye from a 400dpi render of the embedded Figure 5 image (overlaid with a 100px reference grid, corners individually re-cropped and cross-checked — an earlier trace of the NW corner and left edge was caught as wrong this way and corrected before use), then the whole traced shape was uniformly scaled (preserving angles/proportions, no rotation fitted to any known direction) so its enclosed area matches the Application Form's own stated site area exactly: 0.65ha (Q20, 'Please state the site area in hectares (ha): 0.65', matching Q22's greenfield-land figure of the same value). This means: the shape is a genuine hand trace of the real drawing, the area is exact and sourced, but absolute position, scale-per-metre and compass orientation are NOT independently verified against any surveyed coordinate — position error could plausibly be metres, not millimetres. The user's own prior figure for this site ('about 0.62 ha') is close to but not identical to the Application Form's own 0.65ha; 0.65ha (the primary, dated, signed source document's own stated figure) was used for the area-anchor, and the ~0.03ha gap between the two is noted here rather than silently resolved.

Entrance: placed on the southern (Hays Lane) boundary edge at the point where the drawing shows the proposed carriageway meeting the highway — read directly off the same drawing, then projected exactly onto the traced boundary's own south edge (the engine requires the entrance to sit precisely on a boundary edge; the as-traced point was a fraction of a metre off it).

What was modelled as a restriction: only the SuDS infiltration basin (bars='everything', 'Nothing here') — see its own source field.

What was explicitly NOT modelled, stated plainly rather than guessed: the mains sewer and electrical utilities the Planning Statement itself says cross the site ('Due to the presence of the mains sewer running through the northern part of the site, the total usable site area for this proposal is 4167m2' — §4, Principles of development; 'The site is also served by all other necessary infrastructural connections (water, electric and telephone)' — §4, Drainage). No drawing reviewed gives either service's actual route, width or depth — only that the sewer crosses the 'northern part' of the site, which is also broadly where the SuDS basin restriction above already sits. Placing a second, undimensioned corridor on top of that would be inventing a position and width the source material doesn't support, not tracing one — so, consistent with how Meads' own un-locatable sewer easement was handled, it is left out rather than guessed. Note for interpreting the engine's result: the real scheme's own 4167m2 'usable' figure (from a 6500m2 gross site) implies roughly 2333m2 of the site is already treated as unbuildable by the applicant's own numbers for sewer + SuDS combined — materially more than the ~340m2 SuDS-only polygon modelled here, so the engine's houses-only search still has more nominally 'free' land northward than the real scheme assumed it had.

South frontage (observed, not modelled as a restriction): the same drawing shows a new 2.5m public pavement along Hays Lane and an existing hedge bank translocated to sit behind it (Appendix 1, Translocation Method Statement) — both are already baked into the traced boundary's own southern edge (the pavement strip sits inside the traced site boundary, as drawn), not a separate exclusion zone, since the user did not ask for a bars value on this one and the real scheme's own plots already sit behind it without a dedicated 'keep clear' zone.

Only these three Sageston files were opened for this task (the 'existing site plan' misnamed as Block Plan, the Application Form, and the Planning, Design and Access Statement, whose own embedded Figure 5 supplied the real block plan) — the Phase 1 ecology report, geotechnical/geophysical report, tree survey, consultation responses and application amendments present in the same Drive folder were deliberately not opened for this task, per the user's own instruction.
